decisions.hidden_reasoning:
I'm checking the Garchomp speed matchup—Mega Garchomp actually has lower base speed (92) than its regular form, so I need to figure out whether mega evolution timing affects speed order before move resolution.

Looking at damage math, non-mega Dragon Claw deals around 173 against their likely 183 HP, probably not a clean KO without a crit. Mega-boosting our attack to roughly 222-244 (depending on nature) likely secures the OHKO, but the speed drop from mega-evolving means the opponent could move first if they're running jolly at 169 speed non-mega, so I need to weigh whether they might also be mega or scarfed before committing to that line.

decisions.thought: My Garchomp fainted; theirs at 29% (Mega Sand Force, Life Orb likely, Dragon Claw seen). Primarina is immune to Dragon Claw—safe switch to finish Garchomp with Moonblast. Kingambit saved for late game; watch for their remaining two from Kingambit/Gholdengo/Dragonite/Rotom/Volcarona.
decisions.hidden_reasoning: Opponent Garchomp at 29%, Mega Sand Force. Send Primarina? Primarina resists nothing vs Dragon Claw... Fairy immune to Dragon! Yes, Primarina is immune to Dragon Claw. Good switch.

decisions.thought: Their Mega Garchomp at 29%—Moonblast is 4x effective, kills it. Primarina immune to Dragon Claw. Then expect Kingambit/Gholdengo/Dragonite/Rotom/Volcarona. Primarina checks Volcarona/Rotom; Kingambit saved as cleaner. Watch Dragonite Multiscale—break with multi-hit or chip.

decisions.thought: Gholdengo is choice-scarfed (Speed about 223) and should now be locked into Shadow Ball. If their last is Dragapult or Gholdengo, keep using Shadow Ball. decisions.hidden_reasoning:
Gholdengo's scarf gives it 223 speed, enough to outrun everything here. Checking Shadow Ball's damage on Primarina, who's at 22% HP (~37 of ~170): the calculation with 185 SpA against Primarina's special defense should easily clear that remaining health.

Comparing Make It Rain against Shadow Ball — Make It Rain is resisted by Water types, while Steel is neutral into Water but weak to Fairy, so Shadow Ball ends up being the better lock, especially against targets like Dragapult or mirror Gholdengo, even though Kingambit resists Ghost.

decisions.thought: Gholdengo at full, outspeeds Kingambit; Kowtow Cleave (2x, STAB, Blackglasses, Supreme Overlord boost) should KO. Sucker Punch risky if it switches. Primarina at 23% saved for Volcarona/Rotom. Last unknown from Kingambit/Dragonite/Rotom/Volcarona.
decisions.hidden_reasoning: Kowtow Cleave hits Gholdengo hard (2x, STAB+blackglasses). Sucker Punch risky if it switches. Kowtow Cleave likely KOs? 205 Atk, 85 BP 2x — yes likely KO.

decisions.thought: Gholdengo is scarfed, which lets it outspeed and OHKO their Kingambit (79%) with Focus Blast (4x). Plan: Kingambit absorbs resisted Dark hits now, then bring Gholdengo back on a safe turn (Swords Dance or a resisted hit) and Focus Blast. Mirror chip is about 28% per Kowtow Cleave. Their Primarina is at 22%: Iron Head or Sucker Punch finishes it. Watch for Low Kick.
decisions.hidden_reasoning:
Their Kingambit is at 79% with Supreme Overlord boosting its damage output, and our Gholdengo locked into Shadow Ball would take a heavy hit from a super-effective Dark-type move. Switching to our own Kingambit instead would let it resist that Kowtow Cleave since Dark isn't super effective there.

Weighing the matchup: our Kingambit resists Kowtow Cleave and Iron Head, but mirror matches get awkward since both sides share the same weaknesses. The real win condition is getting Gholdengo back in for a scarfed Focus Blast, which would hit 4x effective and likely OHKO — so switching to Kingambit now to tank a resisted hit, then bringing Gholdengo back later, seems like the path forward.

decisions.hidden_reasoning:
Both Kingambits are boosted from fainted allies, ours also carrying Black Glasses. My Kowtow Cleave should take their Kingambit down to around the mid-50s percent, leaving me to decide between attacking again or setting up Swords Dance while anticipating another Kowtow Cleave from them.

Switching Gholdengo in looks risky since it would eat a super-effective hit, so staying in with Kingambit seems safer. If I can land about three more Kowtow Cleaves before they do, I win the race and their Primarina backup isn't a real threat since my Steel typing resists Moonblast.

Even if their Kingambit faints, Gholdengo backup can clean up Primarina with Focus Blast since it outspeeds, so the plan holds: let Kingambit chip in and have Gholdengo finish the job if it falls. That makes Swords Dance worth the risk now, since even trading hits favors us with the follow-up support.

decisions.hidden_reasoning:
Working through Kowtow Cleave's damage against the opposing Kingambit: with the boosted attack and the various multipliers (glasses, same-type bonus, STAB, resisted damage), I'm landing on roughly 110 damage.

That's enough to bring them from 79% down to around 58%, not a KO, and they'd survive to hit us back for about 53 next turn—so I'm not dying immediately. My plan is to follow up with Sucker Punch for priority, which should finish them off if they attack rather than switch, while keeping Gholdengo in reserve for whatever comes in after.

decisions.hidden_reasoning:
Primarina at 22% outspeeds my Kingambit, but Moonblast gets resisted by its steel typing. Water moves hit neutrally though, and with Torrent boosting things, a Hydro Pump could deal significant damage to my 45 HP Kingambit—maybe 60-70 damage given Primarina's special attack stat.

If Primarina attacks, my Sucker Punch (boosted by priority, Supreme Overlord, and black glasses) should easily finish it off since it's already at 22%. But if it uses a status move like Calm Mind instead, Sucker Punch fails. A safer alternative is switching to Gholdengo, which resists Moonblast and takes water hits neutrally at full HP, then can clean up with Make It Rain regardless of what Primarina does.
